# Reset54

> Peter Hay is an independent strategic advisor and fractional advisor based in the UK. He works with senior leaders in complex organisations when direction is uncertain, progress has stalled, or the problem itself is not yet fully clear. His approach is to step back, understand what is really happening beneath the surface, and restore clarity, direction and momentum without increasing pressure.

Reset54 Ltd, founded by Peter Hay, provides independent strategic advisory services. Contact: peter.hay@reset54.co.uk | LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/peterhay/

## About Peter Hay

Peter Hay has over 20 years of experience working alongside leaders navigating complex change. He operates as a thinking partner: moving comfortably between the detail and the wider system, close enough to understand the reality of decisions and delivery, while creating the clarity needed to restore direction.

His advisory is strengthened by practical use of AI across customer enablement, research synthesis, workshop preparation, service blueprinting, rapid prototyping and decision support. He works best with experienced, capable leaders who find themselves in situations where pushing harder is no longer the answer.

He does not offer fixed packages or predefined methodologies. Every engagement starts with understanding what is actually happening and deciding together what kind of support would be most useful.

## Services

- **Independent strategic advisory** – Thinking partnership for senior leaders navigating complex change
- **Fractional advisor** – Retained or fractional involvement where ongoing external perspective is needed
- **Strategic clarity** – Rapid sense-making when direction is uncertain or progress has stalled
- **Transformation support** – Helping complex organisations move from ambiguity to evidence and momentum

## Selected clients

PepsiCo, Mastercard, Lloyds Commercial Bank, Southern Water, Calor Gas, Fulham Pier, The Big Issue

## Project highlights

### PepsiCo – data trust and efficiency
R&D teams relied on disconnected systems to access flavour and seasoning data, creating duplication of work, manual effort to combine data, growing mistrust in reports and no clear ownership across systems. Peter mapped the system, identified value losses by working directly with R&D stakeholders, and built a grounded business case. Outcome: 5,000+ hours of efficiency opportunity identified; clear path to a connected data ecosystem; improved data trust and usability.

### Mastercard – global product governance
Siloed teams across regions, limited visibility for leaders, no shared definition of success, and increasing delays created barriers to product development across 12 global business units. Peter aligned 12 global product groups, defined Materiality, Velocity and Quality metrics, created practical decision tools and removed friction from governance. Outcome: 3 years saved in development timelines; 70% global alignment achieved; faster decision-making across the organisation.

### Lloyds Commercial Bank – commercial customer onboarding
A 6-month onboarding process for new commercial customers was underpinned by fragmented systems and poor customer experience. Peter introduced agile and lean experimentation to test solutions with real customers, then scaled within a newly formed embedded innovation lab. Outcome: onboarding reduced from 6 months to 7 days; new ways of working embedded across the organisation.

### Southern Water – innovation capability
No internal innovation capability, slow delivery processes and rising pressure from ageing infrastructure created significant business risk. Peter co-designed and ran an innovation capability with a team of 12, launching live experiments within 3 months. Outcome: £25m savings; improved organisational resilience; internal team upskilled to continue independently.

### Fulham Pier – digital placemaking
A major riverside destination had to be designed while construction was still under way, with significant ambiguity around customer journeys, operational workflows and supplier priorities. Peter translated the destination vision into a connected end-to-end digital placemaking experience. Outcome: critical day-one journeys prioritised; third-party suppliers aligned around a shared delivery blueprint; phased digital roadmap created.

### Calor Gas – legacy process redesign
A core customer process unchanged since 1935 was misaligned with modern customer needs, with limited visibility of operational issues. Peter conducted comprehensive customer and stakeholder research, mapped the complete end-to-end journey and created new solution concepts. Outcome: clear visibility into process failures; stakeholder alignment on required changes; foundation for complete process redesign.

### The Big Issue – digital and financial inclusion
Growing risk that vendors would be excluded from digital financial systems as society became increasingly cashless. Peter conducted ethnographic research to understand real barriers and translated needs into a viable service model. Outcome: beta product designed and live pilot shipped to vendors in 10 weeks.

## The common thread across engagements

- Complex problems that span multiple teams and functions
- Legacy systems and processes that no longer serve modern needs
- Data fragmentation and loss of trust in existing information
- Decision-making bottlenecks that slow commercial progress
- Frontline teams disconnected from strategic direction
- Previous attempts at change that have not delivered results
